Newron Amends Terms of EUR 38 Million Financing
The Italian pharmaceutical company has agreed with its investor group to modify the third tranche of its up to EUR 38 million financing agreement.
Updated on Nov. 27, 2026 in Corporate Finance
Newron has agreed with the investor group participating in its up to EUR 38 million financing to amend certain terms of the third tranche, corresponding to gross proceeds of EUR 5.5 million. Under the amendment, the investor group will subscribe to the third tranche no later than December 31, 2026, with shares issued at a formula-based price.
Why it matters
The amendment adjusts how a portion of Newron's funding is raised while the company continues developing evenamide in its global pivotal ENIGMA-TRS Phase 3 program. The changes bear on the company's capital position as it advances a late-stage clinical program.
The third tranche carries gross proceeds of EUR 5.5 million, with a subscription deadline of December 31, 2026, and a further EUR 12 million expected only if ENIGMA-TRS results are positive. The subscription price follows an agreed formula, and the final share count is not specified in the announcement.
The players
Newron Pharmaceuticals S.p.A.
Newron is a Bresso, Italy-based pharmaceutical company developing evenamide for schizophrenia and marketing safinamide under the Xadago brand for Parkinson's disease.
The details
Newron's investor group will settle the third tranche through newly issued shares, priced under an agreed formula. The amendment modifies certain terms of the financing agreement originally signed in February 2026, and the company says the proceeds are expected to fund global ENIGMA-TRS studies and extend its cash runway beyond the pivotal 12- and 26-week results.
Timeline
February 2026: Original up to EUR 38 million financing agreement signed.
November 27, 2026: Newron announces the amended financing terms.
December 31, 2026: Deadline for the investor group to subscribe to the third tranche.
Market Dynamics
The financing structure ties additional investor capital to the readout of the ENIGMA-TRS Phase 3 program, so the company's funding depends in part on that trial's outcome. The EUR 12 million conditional subscription makes the trial result a direct driver of the company's near-term capital.
Shareholders in Newron should note that new shares will be issued to the investor group under the formula-based price, which may dilute existing holdings. The conditional EUR 12 million tranche means future share issuance also depends on trial results.
The takeaway
Financing tied to clinical milestones shifts risk onto both the company and its investors, so the outcome of the ENIGMA-TRS study will determine whether the additional capital is raised. Readers following Newron should track the trial readout and the subscription deadline.
What happens next
The investor group's subscription to the third tranche is due by December 31, 2026, and the additional EUR 12 million subscription is expected once ENIGMA-TRS results are disclosed.

Healthleap Raises $38M to Help Hospitals Find Patients with Undiagnosed Conditions
Healthleap Screens Every Adult Inpatient, Every Day, at More Than 50 Hospitals, Including Penn Medicine, Houston Methodist, Cedars-Sinai, and Emory Healthcare
Healthleap , a clinical AI platform that screens patients for conditions that often go undiagnosed, today announced $38 million in combined seed and Series A funding from Sequoia Capital, First Round Capital, and Hummingbird Ventures. Healthleap reads each patient’s full record every morning and shows the care team who needs attention first. Patients who would have been missed get seen, and get seen earlier. The funding will help the company to expand to more conditions and grow its engineering, sales, customer success, and product teams.
The Problem: Millions of Patients Leave Hospitals with Undiagnosed Conditions
Hospitals today are overwhelmed with understaffed clinical teams and manual screening processes. This creates a cycle of worse health outcomes and systemic financial loss. Consider malnutrition: Most hospitals still screen for it with two questions that a nurse asks once, at admission. Patients who are sedated, confused, or too sick to answer are the ones most likely to be missed. Up to half of hospitalized patients are at risk , yet fewer than 9% are formally diagnosed , contributing to increased morbidity, mortality, length of hospital stay, and cost. When malnutrition is diagnosed and treated, it leads to better health outcomes, and hospitals can claim ~$11,000 in reimbursement for each severe malnutrition diagnosis. One Penn Medicine hospital observed that Healthleap drove $23.8M a year from a combination of incremental reimbursement revenue and the financial impact of length-of-stay reductions.
“Every week, millions of patients leave hospitals with unresolved health conditions that will erode their health and cost up to 10x more to treat later,” explained Josiah Meyer, Co-Founder and CEO at Healthleap…

articles.title: Icarus Raises $25M for Solar-Powered Stratospheric Aircraft It Calls a Modern-Day U-2
articles.snippet: Icarus Raises $25M for Solar-Powered Stratospheric Aircraft It Calls a Modern-Day U-2 Wowtale
articles.text:
Icarus , a U.S. startup that builds solar-powered unmanned aircraft to fly in the stratosphere for reconnaissance and communications, has raised $25 million. In a LinkedIn post on Thanksgiving, November 26, CEO Henry Kwan announced the round and described the company as building “the modern-day U2 spy plane,” pitched as autonomous, solar-powered and low-cost. The U-2 is the high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft the United States has flown since the Cold War. The investors, the round’s stage and the valuation were not disclosed.
Kwan thanked investors, the team, partners and customers in turn, and gave the credit to his team. After late nights, 4 a.m. starts for Mojave and deployments around the world, he wrote, it was the team that built the aircraft and put it at 70,000 feet (about 21,000 meters). The money will go toward Phase 1 of what he called the “Secret Icarus Master Plan”: building small, affordable solar-powered aircraft for intelligence and communications. Phases 2 to 4 were left unexplained (“If you know, you know”). The company says it wants more builders, more production and more flights, with better reliability, faster deployments and lower costs, and it is still hiring.
The gap that satellites, balloons and aircraft leave open
Icarus’s aircraft is called APOLLO. It is a solar-powered unmanned aircraft designed to fly at 60,000 feet (about 18,000 meters) and above. According to a U.S. Army newsletter, it is a low-cost, mass-producible platform that stays aloft for long periods to provide persistent sensing, communications relay and data backhaul. The company says a single aircraft can monitor up to 7,500 square kilometers and send data with a latency of 5 to 10 milliseconds.
The technology targets the space that satellites, balloons and ordinary aircraft leave open. A satellite follows a fixed orbit, so an adversary knows when it passes overhead. A balloon drifts with the wind. A conventional aircraft burns fuel for as long as it is in the air. A solar-powered stratospheric aircraft can stay over one area for a long time. Taro Fukuyama, an Icarus investor, made the same argument in a post on X explaining why he invested , and put the price of an aircraft at around $100,000.
Icarus was founded in 2023, started out in a garage in El Segundo, near Los Angeles, and joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch. Its record with the U.S. Army stands out. According to an Army FUZE newsletter , Icarus took first place and a $25,000 prize at the Army’s xTech|Live competition at SOF Week in 2025 and won another $30,000 at xTech|Search 9. It then landed a Phase I Army Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) contract worth up to $250,000 and took part in the Valiant Shield exercise in Guam in June. Along the way APOLLO moved from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 3 to 7, on a scale where 1 is basic research and 9 is fielded operation, and the four engineers who entered the competition grew into a team of about 50.
Kwan, the founder, studied aerospace engineering at Georgia Tech. According to his YC profile , he built drones for NASA and worked on satellites at Orbital.
Money is already pouring into reconnaissance and surveillance
Icarus is not alone in the stratosphere. Sceye received an investment from SoftBank as the first tranche of its Series C to scale its stratospheric platform, and Skydweller, which builds solar-powered long-endurance aircraft, and Airbus-backed AALTO compete in the same field.

Vector Singularity raises second round within six months as Alibaba makes first quantum computing investment
Add preferred source
Vector Singularity, a neutral-atom quantum computing company founded just six months ago, announced the completion of a several-hundred-million-yuan Series A round led by the Beijing Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund and Beijing Industrial Development Investment Management, with participation from Alibaba Group and China Merchants Venture Capital. It marks Alibaba's first investment in a quantum computing company. Founder Li Xiangliang studied under a scholar in cold-atom quantum simulation, and the team now has nearly 20 full-time PhDs. The company is pursuing rubidium and ytterbium atomic routes in parallel and plans to release its first-generation prototype and a QAgent product in the first half of 2027. Since November, the neutral-atom sector has seen multiple hundred-million-yuan financings, as the industry shifts from hype to rational scrutiny.
Key Elements
Vector Singularity Li Xiangliang Alibaba Beijing Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences China Merchants Venture Capital China Telecom Quantum Information Technology Group neutral-atom quantum computing Yuanji Quantum Atom Matrix
Amid a capital winter, the quantum computing sector has drawn a headline-grabbing deal. Beijing Vector Singularity Technology Co. (Vector Singularity), founded just six months ago, announced the completion of a Series A round worth several hundred million yuan (approximately $45 million), led by the Beijing Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund, Beijing Industrial Development Investment Management and its Beijing Industrial Quantum Fund, Beijing Wanxin Rongzhi, and the Zhongguancun Science City Fund, with participation from Alibaba Group, China Merchants Venture Capital, Qifu Capital, Hunan Caixin, Beiyang Haitang Fund, and Yarui Capital. It is Alibaba's first foray into quantum computing, and Vector Singularity's second funding round in less than six months, following an angel round of more than 100 million yuan (approximately $15 million) in August.
Vector Singularity was incubated by the Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences and focuses on complete neutral-atom quantum computing systems, measurement and control systems, and supporting algorithms. Founder and CEO Li Xiangliang studied at Tsinghua University for his bachelor's and master's degrees and earned his doctorate at ETH Zurich under Tilman Esslinger, a scholar in cold-atom quantum simulation. After returning to China at the end of 2021, he joined the Beijing academy to lead construction of a ytterbium-atom quantum computing platform. According to the company, nearly 20 PhDs have joined full time, covering key areas including atom manipulation, precision optics, experimental control, and quantum error correction.
Neutral atoms are one of the main technical routes in quantum computing, using lasers to trap and manipulate atoms so they serve as qubits. Atoms of the same species are naturally identical, and optical tweezers can flexibly arrange and move them, offering room to scale up computing power, though the system still must address computational errors and stability. Discovery Bank raises 2029 client target to three million as expansion gathers pace
Zanele Songo | Published 1 day ago
Ask AI
Discovery Bank is targeting three million clients by 2029 as it prepares to expand into family and SME banking in 2027.
Image: Discovery Bank
Discovery Bank has raised its customer growth ambitions after exceeding expectations, with the lender now targeting three million clients by 2029 as it prepares to expand into family and small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) banking in 2027.
The bank expects to reach two million clients by the end of its 2027 financial year, two years ahead of its original target, according to Discovery’s Capital Markets Day presentation on Thursday.
The financial services group has consequently increased its 2029 client target from two million to three million, an increase of 50%, as it looks to capitalise on the growing adoption of its digital banking platform.
Discovery Group chief executive Adrian Gore said the bank’s performance had exceeded expectations, with customer acquisition accelerating as the business gained scale.
“The performance of the bank has been quite staggering,” Gore said. “We think we will get to the two million customers by the end of this financial year, by June 2027.”
Gore added that the group was increasing its client target to three million by 2029, while retaining its R3 billion operating profit ambition.
Customer growth drives expansion
Discovery Bank had close to 1.6 million clients at the end of its 2026 financial year, with retail deposits of R27 billion and advances of just under R13 billion.
The bank is currently onboarding approximately 1,800 new clients daily, with about 70% of them coming from outside the Discovery Group.
Discovery Bank CEO Hylton Kallner said the bank’s growth strategy was supported by its full-service digital banking model, which combines transactional banking, savings, investments and lending with Discovery’s broader financial services offering.
"We were very explicit. Discovery Bank would be built on a full-service offering," Kallner said.
The bank’s strategy also relies on using data and artificial intelligence to personalise banking experiences, improve customer service and strengthen protection against fraud.
Kallner said one of the bank’s priorities was to use its technology capabilities to deliver a more personalised experience.
“To utilise the data and the AI and the capabilities that we’ve built to personalise the entire bank, to personalise the experience, to scale it efficiently, to protect clients, and to offer best-in-class service to our banking clients,” he said.
Family and SME banking planned for 2027
The bank plans to expand its product offering into family banking and SME banking during 2027, opening up additional customer segments beyond its existing retail banking market.
“Over the course of the next year, we will be expanding in areas of family banking. We will be expanding into areas like SME banking. We see significant opportunities in these adjacencies,” Kallner added.
The move into SME banking could position Discovery to compete more directly in the small-business banking market, where businesses require transactional accounts, payment solutions and access to finance.
However, the bank has not yet detailed the specific products, services or financing facilities that will form part of its SME offering.

articles.title: Why Elon Musk's plan for 1 million AI satellites is raising concerns
articles.snippet: Why Elon Musk's plan for 1 million AI satellites is raising concerns The Economic Times
articles.text:
Synopsis
SpaceX's pitch is to take the impact of data centres away from Earth, using a million solar-powered satellites to do AI data crunching in space and beam the results to Earth. But what is the impact of one million satellites, both in space and on Earth? Why has the Federal Communications Commission made this decision? And will a million satellites actually end up in orbit?
Listen to this article in summarized format Listen
Agencies
This week, on the eve the Thanksgiving holiday, the United States Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX 's plan to launch one million " Starmind " artificial intelligence (AI) data centre satellites .
This decision reflects the convergence of a satellite boom, an AI bubble and the Trump administration's disregard for environmental regulation.
If Starmind proceeds in full, the number of operational satellites will be multiplied by a factor of 50. Space and our night skies will become vastly busier places.
SpaceX's pitch is to take the impact of data centres away from Earth, using a million solar-powered satellites to do AI data crunching in space and beam the results to Earth.
But what is the impact of one million satellites, both in space and on Earth? Why has the Federal Communications Commission made this decision? And will a million satellites actually end up in orbit?
Ups and downs
We are currently in a satellite boom, and constellations of hundreds or thousands of satellites are a key feature.
The Starlink internet satellites (another SpaceX project) is the best known example of such a constellation. Orbital rocket launches have increased to almost one per day, while the number of operational satellites is creeping towards 20,000.
But Starmind represents something else. A million satellites.
To get so many satellites into orbit would be a vast undertaking. If the satellites have a lifetime of five years (similar to Starlink satellites), then roughly 500 satellites would need to be launched every day.
This also implies that roughly 500 satellites would eventually need to be disposed of every day. For satellites less than 2,000 kilometres above Earth, disposal usually means reentry and burning up in the atmosphere. And this has consequences.
When satellites burn up in the atmosphere, their materials react with and are deposited into the upper atmosphere. We now have satellites depositing far more aluminium, titanium, copper and lead into the atmosphere than the natural quantities from meteors.
Aluminium is of particular concern, as alumina can lead to the destruction of ozone in the upper atmosphere. This could increase ultraviolet light on Earth and the risk of skin cancers.
It's getting busy
Increasing the number of satellites by a factor of 50 is going to change our view of the sky.
If you look up during the early evening, you will see the stars your ancestors saw. But within a minute or two you will see a satellite. A point of light silently moving from horizon to horizon.
Our view of the night skies could fundamentally change.
Each satellite would be 75 metres wide and in the early evening they will be brighter than any star. And with a million satellites in orbit, there will be hundreds of Starmind satellites above the horizon irrespective of where you are.

Written by Huang Nan

36Kr has learned that Cangchao Technology, a surface intelligent driving company, recently closed a tens of millions of yuan Angel++ round of financing, co-invested by Industrial Securities' subsidiary Industrial Securities Capital and listed company Gaohua Technology. This marks the third round of financing completed by the company in 2026. The funds will be mainly invested in digitalization and product implementation of offshore operation and maintenance scenarios, marine physics AI technology R&D, classification society certification and industry standard formulation, while promoting cutting-edge exploration of the offshore world model.
After the completion of this round of financing, together with the previous series of seed round, Angel round and Angel+ round financing, Cangchao Technology's total financing amount has reached nearly 100 million yuan. The seed round was funded by Lianyungang Ocean Fund, the investors of the Angel round include Yungang Group, Tianhui Capital and Lianyungang Financial Holding Group, and the investor of the Angel+ round is Haizhou Bay Development Group.
Cangchao Technology was established at the end of 2023, with its headquarters located in Lianyungang. The company focuses on the offshore embodied intelligent track, takes "marine physics AI" as its technical base, and has built a three-layer product architecture covering underlying algorithms, full-vessel products and shore-based control. The bottom layer is the self-developed marine physics AI system, with the intelligent navigation AI brain "OceanHub" as the core; on this basis, three series of unmanned vessels including Lan, Yu and Yao, as well as the OceanHub on-board intelligent driving solution have been derived. This architecture enables the surface intelligent driving capability to adapt to different ship types, sea areas and operation scenarios.
The team is composed of professionals in cutting-edge technical fields such as ship engineering, underwater robots and commercial aerospace, and the core members have cross-professional backgrounds in both ship design and surface autonomous driving. Cheng Chen, founder and CEO of the company, holds a doctorate degree from Hohai University, once served as an external technical consultant for multiple local maritime administrations, and deeply participated in a number of national key R&D projects.
